newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HARMONY ALLOWED TO MARKET A THIRD OWN GOLD.
newsitem.headline: HARMONY ALLOWED TO MARKET A THIRD OWN GOLD.

text.p: South Africa's Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd said on Thursday it had received Reserve Bank approval to market internationally a third of its gold production, amounting to eight tonnes a year.
This is the first time a South African producer has been allowed to sell its gold direct, rather than via the central bank.

Harmony, part of Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd , said permission had been granted with immediate effect but it would only start selling gold independently when its existing refining agreement with Rand Refinery ends in October this year.
The decision to allow Harmony to sell part of its output direct follows the mine's recent announcement that it is to establish its own commercial-scale gold refinery.
Work on the refinery, which is scheduled for completion in the third quarter, is already under way at the mine.

Managing director Bernard Swanepoel welcomed the partial exchange control exemption granted by the Reserve Bank but said he hoped Harmony would eventually be allowed to market its full production of around 24 tonnes a year.

"At least we are now in a position to finalise negotiations with potential international partners regarding the eight tonnes of gold per year which the Reserve Bank has put at our disposal," he said in a statement.
Options under consideration include marketing gold bullion in the form of kilo bars as well as the establishment of a local gold jewellery manufacturing business.
